title: bug: the compose-managed incumbent still carries every variable value in its docker inspect output
description:
Filed from task-0ca117e389df43ee9b458255f0752842, whose architect invited the filing rather than the widening.

THE ASYMMETRY. That row made the deployed CANDIDATE receive its environment through a bind-mounted file specifically so no value lands in `docker inspect .Config.Env` — measured: `--env` gives 1 grep hit for a planted value, a mounted file gives 0. The INCUMBENT is unchanged and is not held to that standard: `docker-compose.override.yml` delivers `DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:?set DATABASE_URL in .env}` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` to the compose `app` and `db` services, so the same values sit in THEIR `Config.Env` and are printed by `docker inspect` to anyone who can reach the docker socket.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE TODAY. `tests/e2e/foundation/platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts` sweeps `docker inspect <candidate>` (:218) and never sweeps the incumbent or the db container. So its `hits=0` result — and any epic claim resting on it that "no secret surfaces anywhere along the pipeline" — is true of the CANDIDATE only. The sweep is not wrong; its scope is just narrower than the sentence it is quoted for.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not prescribed: either extend the canary's sweep to the compose-managed containers and make the generated compose topology deliver by mounted file too, or narrow the epic's DoD-5 wording to say explicitly which containers were swept. Do NOT weaken the existing candidate sweep either way.

Not urgent: `.env` is already gitignored and excluded from every build context, so this is a local-socket exposure rather than a committed or published one. LOW.
definitionOfDone: Either the compose-managed app and db containers stop carrying variable values in docker inspect, or the epic's secrecy claim states in writing which containers the canary sweeps and which it does not.
The candidate-inspect sweep at platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts:218 is unchanged or strengthened, never narrowed.
If the sweep is extended, its swept=N count line rises and the new artifacts are named in the assertion message, as every other sweep in that file already is.

MEASURED — THE ENTRYPOINT TRAP, live, on a real built product image (`moecanaryeafdb4b2-app:latest`, left by an earlier canary run), read exactly the way `imageCommandArgv` (deploy-candidate-environment.ts:148) does:

So the node base image DOES contribute `docker-entrypoint.sh` even though the generated Dockerfile sets none. THE DESIGN ANSWER: set `command:` ONLY and never `entrypoint:`. `command:` replaces `.Config.Cmd` and LEAVES `.Config.Entrypoint` intact, so docker-entrypoint.sh needs no restoring and the trap is avoided by construction rather than worked around. (node's docker-entrypoint.sh prepends `node` only when $1 starts with `-` or is not on PATH; `/bin/sh` is neither, so it `exec "$@"`s our loader unchanged.) Step 3 will land this as an assertion pair — the override emits no `entrypoint:` key, and its `command:` is derived from DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH — rather than a comment.

MEASURED — COMPOSE INTERPOLATION WILL EAT THE LOADER unless escaped. Compose interpolates `$VAR`/`${VAR}` in the compose file and reports `invalid interpolation format` on a bare `$` before `(`. So the emitted loader must write `$$` for every literal `$`: `export DATABASE_URL="$$(cat /run/secrets/database_url)"`. Using `command:` only means the loader needs no `$0`/`$@` at all (it execs the entry path directly), so there is exactly ONE escape to get right instead of three. Verified live in step 5.

implementationPlan.description: Stop the app service delivering DATABASE_URL through compose `environment:`, in deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts. Replace that one line with a compose SECRET whose value still comes from `.env`, plus an entrypoint that loads it — the same shape the deployed candidate already uses, so the two paths stop disagreeing about what a secret is. Target shape: the app service keeps `PORT` in `environment:` (a port is not a secret), gains `secrets: [database_url]`, and a top-level `secrets: { database_url: { environment: DATABASE_URL } }` block. THE ENTRYPOINT TRAP, and it is the same one the candidate hit: setting `entrypoint:` in compose CLEARS the image's command, exactly as `--entrypoint` clears `.Config.Cmd`, so the service MUST also name `command:` explicitly or it starts with nothing to exec. Derive that `command:` from the `DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH` constant already in this file rather than retyping the path, so the Dockerfile's `CMD` and the override cannot drift apart. MEASURE, do not assume, whether the node base image's own `docker-entrypoint.sh` must be restored ahead of it — read the built image's `Entrypoint ++ Cmd` with `docker image inspect` the way `imageCommandArgv` does, and make the answer an assertion rather than a comment. The loader itself must put NO value in any argv: `export DATABASE_URL="$(cat /run/secrets/database_url)"; exec "$0" "$@"` names a path only. PRESERVE THE FAIL-FAST: `${DATABASE_URL:?set DATABASE_URL in .env}` makes compose refuse with a readable message today, and `secrets.environment` takes no `:?` form, so an unset variable would silently start the app with an empty connection string. Keep an equivalent and prove it with an arm.

DESIGN DECISION, AND IT DEPARTS FROM THE STEP TEXT — `command:` ONLY, NO `entrypoint:`. The step prescribed "an entrypoint that loads it" plus an explicit `command:`. Measured on a real built product image left by an earlier canary run (`moecanaryeafdb4b2-app:latest`), read exactly as `imageCommandArgv` does:
  docker image inspect --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}\n{{json .Config.Cmd}}'
  ["docker-entrypoint.sh"]
  ["node","/app/dist/server.js"]
So the trap is real. But `command:` replaces `.Config.Cmd` and LEAVES `.Config.Entrypoint` ALONE, which avoids the trap by construction instead of working around it: docker-entrypoint.sh needs no restoring, and the "must the base image's own entrypoint be restored ahead of it" question the step asked me to measure is answered NO, because nothing clears it. Confirmed on a live container below: `.Config.Entrypoint` came back `["docker-entrypoint.sh"]` with the override in force. Second benefit — the loader needs no `$0`/`$@`, so there is ONE `$` to escape rather than three. The step's stated invariant (no value in any argv, entry path derived from DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH not retyped) is fully honoured: `DATABASE_URL_LOADER` interpolates `DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH` and the new `DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_SECRET_PATH`.

THE SECRET FILE IS READABLE BY THE UNPRIVILEGED USER — the risk that would have shown up as a mystery crash, since the generated Dockerfile ends `USER node`. `ls -l /run/secrets/database_url` inside the container: `-r--r--r-- 1 root root 42`, and `id` = `uid=1000(node) gid=1000(node)`. 4. `docker compose config` GREPPED FOR THE VALUE = 0; it resolves the secrets block to `environment: DATABASE_URL` — the NAME. This closes the "inspect is wider than Config.Env / compose config interpolates" risk the plan flagged.

NEW ARM 1 (pure, always runs) — "delivers the app's connection string as a secret, so no value reaches container metadata":
- BIDIRECTIONAL / UNIFORM, and this is the part that answers the bug report's own diagnosis. It iterates the MERGED project — `composeServices(base)` from the leaf's real `docker-compose.yml` producer PLUS `composeServices(override)` — and for EVERY service asserts its `environment:` block carries no `PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN|DATABASE_URL` line, allowing only `*_FILE:` entries whose value is under the derived `/run/secrets` root. Checking only the override is exactly how this leak survived its own canary sweep, so the arm covers both halves and names the offending service in the failure message.
- New helper `serviceSection(body, "    environment:")` reads only the lines under ONE 4-space key and stops at the next key at that depth. Reading the whole service body instead would let a value that moved from `environment:` into `secrets:` keep satisfying an "is it under environment" check — i.e. the arm would go vacuous the moment the fix landed.

- THE ENTRYPOINT TRAP IS NOW AN ASSERTION, which is what step 2 asked for: `expect(override).not.toMatch(/^ {4}entrypoint:/mu)`. Anchored on a YAML KEY at service depth on purpose — the first version used `not.toContain("entrypoint:")` and WENT RED against correct code, because the emitted file's own comment names `entrypoint:` to explain why it is absent. That red is itself a small non-vacuity proof: the arm reads the real emitted bytes.
- DRIFT PIN, one constant across two generators: `command` must contain `exec node ${DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH}` AND the Dockerfile must contain `CMD ["node", "${DEPLOYMENT_ENTRY_PATH}"]`, so the override and the image cannot disagree about what to start.
